title: Students’ future confidence is strongly associated with meaningful schoolwork, teacher recognition, belonging and individualized support
source_unit: Walton Family Foundation–Gallup Voices of Gen Z Study, Engaged Students More Confident in Their Post-High School Future
geography: United States; middle- and high-school students aged 14–19

observations.period: May 22–June 9, 2026; U.S. Gen Z students aged 14–19

denominator.unit: U.S. students aged 14–19 responding to a web survey

future_preparedness.unit: percent agreeing they feel prepared for the future

historical_baseline.unit: percent agreeing they felt prepared in the 2023 first survey

school_interest_gap.value: More than four in ten say school usually does not feel interesting or like a good fit for their talents

observations.method: Walton Family Foundation–Gallup annual web survey of 14–19-year-old Gen Z students, with comparisons to prior annual waves.
observations.uncertainty: The survey is cross-sectional in each wave and the article reports association, not a causal effect of engagement on future preparedness; year comparisons may include sample and context changes.
observations.subgroup: U.S. middle- and high-school students aged 14–19, with comparisons by postgraduation plans and engagement level.
observations.counterinterpretation: Preparedness may influence how students perceive school engagement, or both may reflect family, socioeconomic, school and community conditions; the findings do not isolate teacher or curriculum effects.

high_engagement_prepared.unit: percent of students reporting 10 or more of 12 engaging school experiences who feel prepared for the future

low_engagement_prepared.unit: percent of students reporting three or fewer engaging experiences who feel prepared for the future

engagement_gradient.value: The high-engagement preparedness share is three times the low-engagement share

observations.method: Composite engagement measure covering relevance and interest of coursework, challenge, teacher and peer connection, belonging, recognition and future support.
observations.uncertainty: The 12-experience index is an analytical grouping, not a randomized intervention or validated causal scale; unmeasured student and school characteristics may explain part of the gradient.
observations.subgroup: Students grouped by number of reported engaging school experiences.
observations.counterinterpretation: Highly engaged students may have stronger prior preparation, support or confidence that independently predicts future preparedness; the result should guide mechanism hypotheses rather than prove a school-program effect.

observations.period: May 22–June 9, 2026; belonging and individualized adult support

school_belonging.unit: percent agreeing school is a place where they feel they belong

school_fit.unit: percent agreeing their school feels like the perfect place for students like them

teacher_checkin.unit: percent agreeing a teacher or adult regularly checks in on how they are doing

teacher_recognition.unit: percent agreeing adults at school recognize their individual talents and interests

observations.method: Survey measures on belonging, teacher/adult relationships, recognition, goals and wellbeing support.
observations.uncertainty: Reported relationships and belonging are subjective perceptions and do not measure staff behavior, school climate through observation, or later attainment and retention.
observations.subgroup: U.S. students aged 14–19, including students with different engagement and postgraduation plans.
observations.counterinterpretation: Students may form belonging judgments from broader identity and peer experiences, not only adult support; a supportive teacher relationship may be necessary but insufficient for institutional fit.

denominator.unit: U.S. students aged 14–19, compared by stated postgraduation plans

college_bound_prepared.unit: percent of students planning two- or four-year college who feel prepared for the future

noncollege_prepared.unit: percent of students not planning college who feel prepared for the future

positive_challenge_gap.value: 45% of non-college-bound students versus 67% of college-bound students say schoolwork challenges them in a good way

belonging_gap.value: 59% of non-college-bound students versus 71% of college-bound students feel they belong at school

observations.method: Subgroup comparison by stated postsecondary plans across engagement, belonging, teacher support and preparedness measures.
observations.uncertainty: Postgraduation plans are self-reported and may be correlated with socioeconomic status, achievement, school tracking and family expectations; the survey does not identify the institutional source of the gap.
observations.subgroup: Students planning versus not planning to attend a two- or four-year college.
observations.counterinterpretation: The gap may reflect different pathways and expectations rather than a single failure of school relevance; career and technical pathways could require different forms of engagement that the index does not fully capture.

related_sources.claim: Walton Family Foundation–Gallup research hub describing the annual Gen Z study and related reports.
Foundation knowledge-center context for the 2026 student engagement findings.

boundary: This record adds a U.S. education-and-belonging layer: future confidence is patterned with meaningful schoolwork, teacher recognition, individualized support and belonging, with a notable gap for students not planning college. It is a sponsored cross-sectional web survey and association analysis, not respondent-level longitudinal data, a causal school evaluation, an achievement measure, a clinical assessment or proof that one intervention will close the gap.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official Gallup publication page was retrieved and reviewed for sample, field dates, preparedness trend, engagement gradient, belonging, teacher support and college-plan subgroup findings; the HTML was hashed.
